title: Alcohol and Cannabis. Jointly and Severally
description: Generally, the new concept of  “Cannabis Consumption Lounges”, where adults can smoke, vape etc. cannabis in the presence of other adults, has been...
content_html_sanitized:
Generally, the new concept of  “Cannabis Consumption Lounges”, where adults can smoke, vape etc. cannabis in the presence of other adults, has been presumed to exclude alcohol for a number of reasons.

 

First, it has been hard enough to placate politicians who were leery enough about allowing cannabis consumption anywhere.

 

Second, a lot of cannabis consumers like it, because it is a different “vibe”. No argument.

 

But what about bars that allow cannabis consumption?

 

One of my favorite places in Amsterdam is Barney’s Uptown, a bistro conveniently located across Haarlemerstraat from Barney’s coffee shop, among others.

 

I love having a glass of wine with a joint. In Amsterdam you can’t smoke tobacco in bars and restaurants, but cannabis is up to the owners, and there are a few other places where cannabis smoking is allowed.

 

(Until 2007 there were a number of bars that also sold weed, but the rules were changed and they had to choose one or the other. Most chose cannabis.)

 

Of course, there are millions of cannabis and alcohol consumers who enjoy them at home, both jointly and severally, so to speak, and it’s probably better to toke alone than drink alone. And weed is great for hangovers.

 

More importantly, weed may help alcoholics reduce their alcohol consumption.

See Can Cannabis be Considered a Substitute Medication for Alcohol?

 

Meanwhile, there is a trend away from alcohol consumption generally.

See Sober-Curious: Benefits of an Alcohol-Free Lifestyle

 

Alcohol free beer and wine are the fastest growing segments in Europe and America.

See Low-alcohol beer

At the political level, the alcohol and cannabis industries need to work together and resist politically motivated restrictions pushed by corrupt and/or incompetent politicians.
